the budget talk

copy.title.title:
Faster contract review
for your legal team
copy.title.lead: Legal AI for research and document work: legal sources, your templates and ready drafts in one tool.
copy.starting-point.lead: You are a 4-person legal team at a retail chain, handling around 300 lease agreements and NDAs a month. The previous tool was dropped after 3 weeks as too complicated, so daily work still eats the team’s time.
copy.starting-point.areas:
Lease agreements | Around 300 contracts a month pass through the team, mostly lease agreements and NDAs.
NDAs | NDAs are reviewed one by one, with no shared standard to check them against.
A tool the team keeps using | The previous tool was abandoned after 3 weeks because it was too complicated.
copy.use-areas.solutions:
Lease agreements | Gaius compares the counterparty’s contract with your standards and flags the clauses to change.
NDAs | NDA review against your playbook: you approve a list of deviations instead of reading the whole contract.
A tool the team keeps using | We build skills together with the team in three workshops, on your real matters and to your own standard.
copy.team-support.lead: Your team starts on a 14-day trial on real matters, with workshops and a Legal Engineer to keep it simple.
copy.team-support.concerns: Will the team actually use it? | From the start the tool does what the team does every day, to its own standard, and we train people on their real matters.
copy.tool-comparison.lead: How a general AI chatbot compares with a Legal AI built for work on legal documents.
copy.tool-comparison.rows:
Legal sources | General knowledge, no current case law | Polish and EU law and case law, with case numbers
Your documents | Uploaded one chat at a time | One base of your documents and templates
Confidentiality | Public cloud outside your control | Private environment, never used for training
Verification | Answers without sources | Every answer links to its basis
copy.security.lead: Gaius is hosted in the European Economic Area, and your documents are never used to train models.
